title: Care Management Standard for Transitions of Care After Hospital Discharge
content:
When a Care Management member is discharged from hospital, the member's tier sets how soon the care team follows up, the contact mode the follow-up must use, and how soon medications are reconciled.

## Standard

1. After a hospital discharge the care team follows up within the tier's post-discharge follow-up days, using the tier's required follow-up contact mode.
2. The care team reconciles medications within the tier's medication reconciliation days after the discharge.
3. A discharge from a stay during which the episode was on hold resumes the episode on the discharge date.

Each discharge followed up is recorded once, identified by its discharge date and the hospital, together with the date and mode of the follow-up.

## Condition, judgement and result

| Condition | Judgement | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Member discharged from hospital | Follow-up is due | Follow-up within the tier's days, in the tier's required mode |
| Member discharged from hospital | Medication reconciliation is due | Medications reconciled within the tier's days |
| The episode was on hold during that stay | The stay has ended with the discharge | The episode resumes, on the discharge date |

## Worked dates (hypothetical)

Hypothetical inputs: an episode on hold since the admission on 2 June; discharge on 9 June; a tier with a 3-day follow-up by phone and a 30-day medication reconciliation.

- The episode resumes on 9 June, the discharge date.
- The follow-up is due by 12 June, by phone. A follow-up recorded on 11 June by video does not use the required mode.
- Medications are reconciled by 9 July.

A second hypothetical discharge from another hospital on 20 June is a separate discharge, followed up in its own right within the same number of days.
